To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the improvement in gluco-metabolic status after six months in patients after acute coronary syndromes with abnormal glucose tolerance at discharge was not related to the risk of hospitalization for heart failure.

in pts with acute myocardial infarction, treated invasively: (1) abnormal glucose tolerance (2-hour post load glucose ≥ 7.8 mmol/l) at hospital discharge (3) is associated with higher rate of hospitalization due to decompensated heart failure, and (4) improvement in glucomatoblic status (5) does not influence this rate.

In patients with acute myocardial infection treated invasively there was a trend towards a higher incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in those with abnormal glucose tolerance at discharge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
patients with acute myocardial ischemia, who underwent invasive treatment.
the issue of glucometabolism in the context of the treatment of acute myocardial infraction, in which the most common approach is percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty.
the impact of gluco-metabolic status on the incidence of MACE in patients after AMI treated invasively.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in AMI-pts with AGT at hospital discharge, a more intensive control of glucometabolism is needed.
the improvement of GS in pts with AMI treated invasively is not related to a lower risk of MACE.
in the studied population of AMI-pts the improvement in GS after 6 months of FU was not associated with a better prognosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the improvement of glucometabolism in patients with AMI treated invasively is not related to a reduction in the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events.
there was no significant difference between pAGT-pts, tAGT-pts or newAGT- pts with respect to MACE and heart failure hospitalizations after AMI treated invasively.
there is a need to evaluate the impact of GS at hospital discharge and its improvement after 6 months on long-term outcomes in patients with AMI treated invasively.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the risk of hospitalization for decompensated HF in pts with acute MI and abnormal glucose tolerance at discharge does not change after 6 months of follow-up, despite the improvement in gluco-metabolic status.
the improvement in gluco-metabolic status after hospitalization is associated with a lower risk of hospitalizations due to decompensation of heart failure in AMI-pts.

patients who had normal glucose tolerance at hospital admission and who were diagnosed with newly detected abnormal glucose tolerance at FU-visit were not at higher risk of hospitalization for heart failure.
